#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (icount mode): instruction-count switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Whole-program mode: both legs drain by retired-instruction count alone, with
# no CSR markers in the workload:
#
#   QEMU1 + plugin icount=N1    -> drain at insn N1.
#   vsim --hybrid-icount N2     -> drain N2 insns later.
#
# Workload is the MARKERLESS GEMM twin rt_c_v_matmul_free (200 back-to-back
# 16x16x16 GEMMs, no csrwi 0x7C0). icount IS the only drain trigger -- the
# default CSR matcher has nothing to match. There is no natural end-of-program
# drain here (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count), so it asserts the
# round-trip DRAINS at both ends with both PCs landing inside vmatmul_kernel.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      markerless fixture (default: rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)
#   QEMU_ICOUNT   plugin icount drain target (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   vsim icount drain target  (default: 5000)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"

MODE_LABEL="icount mode (samples a whole-program window)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (markerless RVV GEMM, 200 reps)"
echo "QEMU1 trigger: plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT"
echo "vsim  trigger: --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT  (CSR matcher disabled)"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Resolve the GEMM kernel's address range so the drain checks assert the count
# target landed inside vmatmul_kernel (replaces the old icount_spin's hardcoded
# 0x100002/0x100004 loop PCs). readelf -sW: $2=value(hex) $3=size $8=name.
RE="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
RE="${RE:-riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
read KLO KSZ < <("$RE" -sW "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$8=="vmatmul_kernel"{print strtonum("0x"$2),$3; exit}')
if [ -z "${KLO:-}" ] || [ -z "${KSZ:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: could not resolve vmatmul_kernel range from $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1
fi
pc_in_kernel() { awk -v p="$1" -v lo="$KLO" -v sz="$KSZ" 'BEGIN{exit !(p>=lo && p<lo+sz)}'; }
echo "  vmatmul_kernel: $(printf '0x%x..0x%x' "$KLO" "$((KLO+KSZ))")"

SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-icount-rt.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

echo "[demo icount 1/2] QEMU1 + plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_Q"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU1 drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") (in kernel)"

# vsim resumes from the QEMU drain and attaches the SAME shared mmap so the
# GEMM matrices QEMU1 wrote to .bss survive (mirrors tests/e2e.sh).
echo "[demo icount 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 120 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim state empty"; exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""hsim - end-user entry point for the Andes hybrid simulator.

Single-file driver. Wraps the developer-grade scripts (setup.sh,
tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh) behind four subcommands:

    ./hsim build [--what TARGET]
    ./hsim run <elf-path> --mode csr|pc|icount|slice [--verbose]
    ./hsim test [--filter REGEX] [--mode csr|pc|both]
    ./hsim list <fixtures|demos|modes>
    ./hsim doctor
    ./hsim demo <T1..T7|short-name> [-- KEY=VAL ...]
    ./hsim profile <elf> --slice N --icount M -o BBV
    ./hsim cluster <bbv> --max-k K --simpts P --weights P
    ./hsim archive --state S --mmap M --elf E -o snap/N
    ./hsim replay snap/N [--resume-with vsim|qemu]
    ./hsim estimate <elf> --slice N --icount M --max-k K

Python 3 stdlib only; no pip deps.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


# --- F1: list ---------------------------------------------------------------

# The 4 switching modes. Authoritative source: docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 3 and
# docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md. Kept here so `./hsim list modes` does not
# need to grep the docs at runtime. CSR/PC profile a kernel; icount/SimPoint
# sample the whole program. (bbv / slice / archive / replay are SimPoint stages,
# not top-level modes; the end-of-program exit is the run tail.)
# Tuple: (key, profiles, how-to-run + note).
MODES = [
    ("csr",      "kernel",        "csrwi 0x7C0,{0,1} markers in source (default); ./hsim run --mode csr"),
    ("pc",       "kernel",        "PC / symbol address, no source edit; ./hsim run --mode pc"),
    ("icount",   "whole program", "single boundary at N retired insns, CSR-less; ./hsim run --mode icount"),
    ("simpoint", "whole program", "clustered representative slices -> whole-program cycle estimate; ./hsim estimate"),
]


def parse_fixtures(makefile: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Extract fixture names + family from tests/fixtures/Makefile.

    Returns rows (name, family) in stable, family-grouped order. Family is
    the variable they came from (RT_FIXTURES, RT_C_FIXTURES, ...).
    """
    text = makefile.read_text()
    rows: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    # Variable definitions look like:
    #   RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases \
    #                  rt_long_roi
    # We capture everything up to a non-continuation newline.
    var_pattern = re.compile(
        r"^(?P<var>[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*:?=\s*(?P<body>(?:[^\n]*\\\n)*[^\n]*)$",
        re.MULTILINE,
    )
    interesting = {
        "RT_FIXTURES":      "asm",
        "RT_C_FIXTURES":    "c",
        "RT_C_V_FIXTURES":  "c+rvv",
        "PROBE_V_FIXTURES": "probe",
    }
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for m in var_pattern.finditer(text):
        var = m.group("var")
        if var not in interesting:
            continue

def cmd_demo(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not args.selector:
        print(
            "hsim: missing demo selector -- run ./hsim list demos",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    short, script = _resolve_demo(args.selector)
    if script is None:
        print(
            f"hsim: unknown demo: {args.selector} -- "
            "run ./hsim list demos (or use T1..T7)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    if not script.is_file():
        print(f"hsim: demo script not found: {script}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    env_extra = _parse_demo_passthrough(args.extras)
    if env_extra is None:
        print(
            "hsim: passthrough args must be KEY=VAL form (after `--`)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2

    artifacts = _resolve_artifacts()
    for label, path in artifacts.items():
        if not path.is_file():
            print(f"hsim: {label} not built -- run ./hsim build", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["VSIM_BIN"]    = str(artifacts["vsim"])
    env["VSIM_QEMU"]   = str(artifacts["qemu"])
    env["VSIM_PLUGIN"] = str(artifacts["plugin"])
    # Demos that shell out to RISC-V toolchain binaries (nm, objdump for the
    # PC-mode inner-loop ROI derivation) need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN even when the
    # user hasn't sourced setup.sh first.
    tc = _read_hybrid_toolchain()
    if tc and "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN" not in env:
        env["HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"] = tc
    env.update(env_extra)

    cmd = ["bash", str(script)]
    if args.dry_run:
        for k, v in env_extra.items():
            print(f"{k}={v}")
        print(f"exec: {shlex.join(cmd)}")
        return 0
    return subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env).returncode

# drain here (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count), so it asserts the
# round-trip DRAINS at both ends with both PCs landing inside vmatmul_kernel.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"

MODE_LABEL="icount mode (samples a whole-program window)"

echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (markerless RVV GEMM, 200 reps)"
echo "QEMU1 trigger: plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT"
echo "vsim  trigger: --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT  (CSR matcher disabled)"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Resolve the GEMM kernel's address range so the drain checks assert the count
# target landed inside vmatmul_kernel (replaces the old icount_spin's hardcoded
# 0x100002/0x100004 loop PCs). readelf -sW: $2=value(hex) $3=size $8=name.
RE="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
RE="${RE:-riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
read KLO KSZ < <("$RE" -sW "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$8=="vmatmul_kernel"{print strtonum("0x"$2),$3; exit}')

  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: could not resolve vmatmul_kernel range from $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1
fi
pc_in_kernel() { awk -v p="$1" -v lo="$KLO" -v sz="$KSZ" 'BEGIN{exit !(p>=lo && p<lo+sz)}'; }

STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)

truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_Q"; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo (icount mode): instruction-count switching on the RVV GEMM workload.
#
# Whole-program mode: both legs drain by retired-instruction count alone, with
# no CSR markers in the workload:
#
#   QEMU1 + plugin icount=N1    -> drain at insn N1.
#   vsim --hybrid-icount N2     -> drain N2 insns later.
#
# Workload is the MARKERLESS GEMM twin rt_c_v_matmul_free (200 back-to-back
# 16x16x16 GEMMs, no csrwi 0x7C0). icount IS the only drain trigger -- the
# default CSR matcher has nothing to match. There is no natural end-of-program
# drain here (the demo stops vsim mid-kernel by count), so it asserts the
# round-trip DRAINS at both ends with both PCs landing inside vmatmul_kernel.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      markerless fixture (default: rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf)
#   QEMU_ICOUNT   plugin icount drain target (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   vsim icount drain target  (default: 5000)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_matmul_free}"
QEMU_ICOUNT="${QEMU_ICOUNT:-1000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-1000}"

MODE_LABEL="icount mode (samples a whole-program window)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Fixture: ${FIXTURE} (markerless RVV GEMM, 200 reps)"
echo "QEMU1 trigger: plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT"
echo "vsim  trigger: --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT  (CSR matcher disabled)"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Resolve the GEMM kernel's address range so the drain checks assert the count
# target landed inside vmatmul_kernel (replaces the old icount_spin's hardcoded
# 0x100002/0x100004 loop PCs). readelf -sW: $2=value(hex) $3=size $8=name.
RE="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
RE="${RE:-riscv64-unknown-elf-readelf}"
read KLO KSZ < <("$RE" -sW "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$8=="vmatmul_kernel"{print strtonum("0x"$2),$3; exit}')
if [ -z "${KLO:-}" ] || [ -z "${KSZ:-}" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: could not resolve vmatmul_kernel range from $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1
fi
pc_in_kernel() { awk -v p="$1" -v lo="$KLO" -v sz="$KSZ" 'BEGIN{exit !(p>=lo && p<lo+sz)}'; }
echo "  vmatmul_kernel: $(printf '0x%x..0x%x' "$KLO" "$((KLO+KSZ))")"

SHM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-icount-rt.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHM_SIZE" "$SHM"

read_u64() { python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$1', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek($2); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
"; }

echo "[demo icount 1/2] QEMU1 + plugin icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHM,size=$SHM_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,icount=$QEMU_ICOUNT" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_Q"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: QEMU1 drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU1 drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_Q") (in kernel)"

# vsim resumes from the QEMU drain and attaches the SAME shared mmap so the
# GEMM matrices QEMU1 wrote to .bss survive (mirrors tests/e2e.sh).
echo "[demo icount 2/2] vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT -> drain"
set +e
timeout 120 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHM_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim state empty"; exit 1
fi

PC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 16)
if ! pc_in_kernel "$PC_V"; then
  echo "[demo icount] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") not in vmatmul_kernel"; exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: pc=$(printf '0x%x' "$PC_V") (in kernel)"

# Window cycles: the vsim mcycle delta over the measured window (mcycle@624).
# vsim restores mcycle from the QEMU drain then counts real cycles, so
# vsim - qemu is the window's cycle count.
MC_Q=$(read_u64 "$STATE_Q" 624)
MC_V=$(read_u64 "$STATE_V" 624)
echo "  window_cycles: $((MC_V - MC_Q))  (vsim mcycle=$MC_V - qemu mcycle=$MC_Q)"

echo "[demo icount] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): both drains inside vmatmul_kernel"
